newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B shares end up, A shares down.
newsitem.headline: China's B shares end up, A shares down.

text.p: China's B shares ended sharply higher on Thursday on strong sentiment, with the Shanghai index breaching the key 80-point resistance level and domestic investors the biggest buyers, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index surged 5.522 points or 7.18 percent to 82.392 points on huge volume of 57.12 million shares worth $29.1 million, compared with $15.07 million on Wednesday.
Heavy buying by local speculators gave prices a sudden push up in the afternoon session, brokers said.
Foreign capital was also seen moving into the market, they said.
"With domestic A shares seen as expensive, some domestic players shifted their interest to the B share market, which led to the surge in the B index," one broker said.
The B index, which has moved up sharply in recent months, has been overshadowed by the A index, which is up by more than 40 percent on the start of the year.
Brokers said upward potential would be limited on Friday with technical charts showing signs of a need for a correction.
Huangshan Tourism Development was the star of the day. Institutional buying saw its share price leap $0.066 or 10 percent to $0.726 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Shanghai Chlor Alkai Chemical was the most actively traded, gaining $0.014 or 4.51 percent to $0.324 on volume of 3.4 million shares.
Shenzhen's foreign currency B shares powered to a closing year-high, propelled by strong rises in Shanghai B shares and general optimism about prospects for the market, analysts said.
The index gained 13.77 points or 8.57 percent to close at 174.56 points as turnover hit HK$268.1 million, from Wednesday's HK$89.4 million.
Thursday's surge was led by Wafangdian Bearing Co, which jumped in the morning and was quickly followed by other stocks.
Wafangdian rose HK$0.53 to its daily 10 percent limit-high of HK$5.83 on volume of 2.95 million shares.
Analysts said Wafangdian surged after the Shenzhen-based Securities Times reported its parent company, Wafangdian Bearing Group, would take over a high-technology company, Dalian Instrument Group.
A Wafangdian spokesman said the takeover would have no direct impact on the listed firm.

The Shanghai A share index dipped 7.141 points or 0.51 percent to 1,384.788 points on volume of 695.2 million shares worth 8.5 billion yuan. The SSE30 index fell 21.481 points or 0.60 percent to 3,571.814 points.
Shenzhen's A share index eased 0.04 points or 0.01 percent to 461.31 on turnover of 8.49 billion yuan against Wednesday's 9.02 billion.
